preamble: Between vowels, the voiced retroflex stop [ɖ] lenites to a retroflex lateral [ɭ]: the tongue keeps its curled-back position, but full closure gives way to lateral airflow. In the Rigvedic (Śākala) recitation tradition [ɭ] and [ɭʱ] are the intervocalic realizations of ḍ and ḍh, and Pali shows the same distribution, so Sanskrit forms with -ḍ- correspond to Pali forms with -ḷ-.

examples.note: The Rigveda samhita writes ḷ for intervocalic ḍ; Wiktionary gives the Vedic pronunciation as [iː.ɭ̆ɐi̯].
